advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a runtime/CI guard (or CE cross-check alarm) that flags when any observed per-direction rate approaches or exceeds the hardcoded CEILING, so the upper-bound property cannot silently lapse.
evidence: handler.py:99-106 CEILING = {"InputTokenCount": 6.875e-06, ...} derived 2026-09-25
Comment: 'at parity a price rise would break the upper-bound property silently, on the tick it landed.'
No test or runtime check asserts observed per-token rates remain <= CEILING; re-derivation is a manual `for each direction, max(...)` procedure in a comment.
advisory.finding: The CEILING rate constants are hardcoded in source with a manual re-derivation procedure in a comment and no automated guard or alarm; if a newly-adopted model bills at a higher per-token rate than Claude Opus, the metered arm silently loses its upper-bound property (over-counts becomes under-counts) with no signal, reintroducing the staleness failure mode the change set out to remove — merely relocated from CE-derived state to source constants.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Log (or emit a metric on) CE service keys that were seen but excluded by is_bedrock_service so a new billing-label convention is observable rather than silently dropped.
evidence: handler.py:278 `if not keys or not is_bedrock_service(keys[0]): continue`
handler.py:85 `is_bedrock_service` returns True only for `== 'Amazon Bedrock'` or `.endswith(BEDROCK_EDITION_SUFFIX)`
A service that carries Bedrock spend but is named under a third convention produces no match and no diagnostic — the miss is indistinguishable from 'no Bedrock spend'.
advisory.finding: `_ce_spend_today` classifies grouped CE results with `is_bedrock_service`, silently `continue`-ing on any group whose service key does not match; a genuinely-Bedrock service AWS names without the ' (Amazon Bedrock Edition)' suffix (or not exactly 'Amazon Bedrock') is invisible to the authoritative signal with no error or log, so the authoritative arm can under-read exactly as the old enumerated allowlist did.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Skip or annotate the high-water update when metered.degraded is True so the persisted mark reflects only complete reads, or document that a floored value is intentionally recorded.
evidence: handler.py:479-481 updates high_water whenever `metered is not None and (observed_tokens or prior_high_water is None)` with no check on `metered.degraded`
handler.py:190-191 docstring: 'A partial failure returns degraded=True and a total that is a FLOOR, not the account total.'
Because a nonzero prior_high_water only blocks release, the effect is conservative for release, but a floored value is recorded as if it were an authoritative high-water.
advisory.finding: The high-water mark is updated (state[HIGH_WATER_KEY] = max(...)) even when `metered.degraded` is True — i.e. when the total is an explicit FLOOR from a partial-region read, not the account total. Persisting a floored total as the day's high-water can leave a nonzero mark derived from an incomplete read, which then governs the release gate on later ticks.
